$comment: The source of sf-lookup's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js), written in the standard 1.4 form of five authored files; standard simai.smart-component 1.3.14. The people and object picker: owner decision q-efb6397065 (2026-10-29), UI Chat's request msg-8fbe39bb9acb40b9a08e item 1, design draft control/LOOKUP-FIELD-DESIGN-2026-10-30.md with the consumers' answers msg-41ac91281d8e4852a6f5.

size.summary: The field ladder, as sf-input's: the frame, the padding and the text of the same size; the chips stand on the field's text line, the rows' pictures a rung below.

appearance.summary: How the field looks: a bordered box or a filled one, sf-input's two boxes.

label.summary: The visible name of the field; it names the search box and the list. Without it the host's aria-label does.

placeholder.summary: Shown in the search box while it is empty.

hint.summary: The line under the field; it describes the search box.

name.summary: The form name: one entry with the chosen value, or one entry per chosen value when multiple. Only the values are sent, never the labels.

multiple.summary: Several items, shown as removable chips in the order chosen; the list stays open after a choice. Without it a choice is the value and closes the list.

max-items.summary: Multiple only: the most items that may be chosen (49 for a group). A choice past it is refused with a visible line; 0 is no cap.

min-length.summary: The fewest characters the provider is asked with; below it the list shows the hint and nothing is asked. Inline options are searched at any length.

max-results.summary: The limit the provider is asked for, and the most items one answer shows.

debounce.summary: Milliseconds the field waits after the last key before it asks the provider, as sf-search.

maxlength.summary: The most characters the search box takes (80 for simai.chat); 0 is no limit.

options.summary: A short list given whole, [{value, label, caption?, avatar?}]: searched in place, the provider never asked. A property, or the data-sf-settings island.

exclude.summary: Values left out of every answer and of the inline options (the reader, the current members); the component filters them. A property, or the data-sf-settings island.

provider.summary: The search: async function (query, {cursor, limit, signal}) answering {items: [{value, label, caption?, avatar?: {src} | {initials}}], nextCursor?} or {status: 'unavailable'}; a thrown error or a rejected promise is the error state. The previous call is aborted through signal and its late answer dropped. A property only.

required.summary: The form is not sent while nothing is chosen (value-missing).

disabled.summary: Not searched, not changed, not focusable and not sent with the form; a disabled fieldset does the same.

readonly.summary: The chosen items are shown and sent, but not changed: no search, no remove buttons.

invalid.summary: The page's verdict: the error look and aria-invalid, with error-message under the field.

error-message.summary: Shown in place of the hint while invalid.

value.summary: Single: {value, label} or null. Multiple: a list of {value, label} in the order chosen, [] when nothing is. A chosen item keeps its caption and avatar. Set from code (or the value attribute as JSON; a bare value is read against the options) it says nothing.

input.summary: The value changed: a choice, a chip removed, Backspace in the empty search box. Sent before change, with the same detail; the search box's own input does not leave the host.

change.summary: The value changed by the person, once per choice or removal, as a select's: detail.value is the new value, detail.item the item chosen or removed, detail.action added, removed or replaced. A value set from code, a form reset and a restore say nothing.

relations.name: cl-tag
$comment: The chosen items are sf-tag chips on the field's text line, each with

relations.name: avatars
$comment: A row's picture is the class markup of an avatar (.sf-avatar): a
photo or initials, drawn by the avatars sheet without an element per row.

relations.name: cl-spinner
$comment: The spinner beside Searching... while the provider is asked.

relations.name: cl-button
$comment: Retry after an error and Show more when the answer has a next cursor.

relations.name: icon-buttons
$comment: The clear button of a single field holding a value: the class markup
of an icon button, as sf-rich-text's toolbar draws it.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

accessibility.$comment: The combobox pattern with a list popup: the search box is role combobox with aria-autocomplete list, aria-expanded, aria-controls the listbox and aria-activedescendant the active row; it is named by the label (aria-labelledby) or the host's aria-label and described by the hint or error. The list is role listbox (aria-multiselectable when multiple), its rows role option with aria-selected; the state line under it (hint, searching, nothing found, unavailable, error, the max-items refusal) is role status, polite. ArrowDown and ArrowUp move, Home and End go to the ends while the list is open, Enter chooses, Escape closes and a second Escape clears the query; Backspace in the empty box removes the last chip. Chips are sf-tag with a remove button named Remove <label>.

x-summary: A form field that picks people or objects from a search the host answers: type, see rows with a picture, a name and a caption, choose one or several. Chosen items are removable chips; the list says when it waits for more letters, searches, finds nothing, is unavailable or failed, with a retry.

x-source.brief: UI Chat's request msg-8fbe39bb9acb40b9a08e item 1 (the people picker with server search); owner decision q-efb6397065: a SIMAI Framework component, Apache-2.0

x-decisions: name: sf-lookup, the field renderer's lookup made a component (design draft 2026-10-30). One value model with renderLookupEdit in src/smart/field-renderers: {value, label}, or a list of them when multiple; the renderer is to delegate to sf-lookup in a later pass, not keep a second implementation.

search: the host answers and the component never fetches. provider is a property, a function (query, {cursor, limit, signal}) as sf-search's provider is, so the two read alike. Below min-length nothing is asked and the hint shows; the call waits debounce after the last key; a new call aborts the previous through its signal and an answer that arrives for an older call is dropped, by a sequence number as well as the signal, so a provider that ignores the signal cannot write stale rows.

answers: {items, nextCursor} is results or nothing found; {status: 'unavailable'} the one neutral line (simai.chat sends ACCESS_DENIED for both a disabled catalogue and no rights, and the line says no reason); anything else, a thrown error or a rejected promise, the error line with Retry, which repeats the last call with its cursor. No nextCursor is no Show more: exactly max-results items mean nothing more (consumer answer). An answer longer than max-results is cut to it.

exclude: a list of values taken out of every answer and of the inline options by the component, so a host that cannot filter on its server still never offers the reader or a current member (consumer answer). Values, not items; an item given is read by its value.

options: a short list given whole is searched in place, at any length, by label and caption with case and accents folded; the provider is not asked, as the field renderer's inline lookup does today. With both, options win: a list in hand is the whole set.

choice: chosen items stay in the list, marked (aria-selected and a check) and toggling (consumer answer). Single: a choice replaces the value, commits and closes the list, the search box shows the chosen label; choosing the chosen item changes nothing. Multiple: a choice adds a chip at the end or removes it; past max-items it is refused and a polite line says No more than N instead of ignoring the press (consumer answer).

single display: the chosen label is the search box's text while the person is not searching; typing searches, Escape twice or leaving the field puts the label back, the clear button (Clear) empties the value. A chip for one value would make a single field look like a list of one.

value-from-code: the value property and the value attribute (JSON, or a bare value read against the options) say nothing; a form reset puts the value attribute back and says nothing, restore takes the form's saved entries. Form entries are the values alone: one entry, or one per chosen value through a FormData (§17.1), the labels never.

events: input and change are the native names (§8, §17.3) with a detail {value, item, action}, input first, both once per change the person made. The search box's own input and change stop at the host: typing is not a change of the value. No search event: the provider is the one way the host answers.

states: one line in the list area, role status, polite: the hint (Type at least N characters), the spinner and Searching..., Nothing found, Search is unavailable, the error line with Retry. The words are the language file's, with plural forms for the hint and the refusal.

list surface: the panel is a popover (manual) in the top layer, anchored under the frame with SF.Position at the frame's width, flipped above when there is no room, as sf-dropdown's list; it stays inside the element, so focus leaving the element closes it without a document listener. Rows are the class markup of the avatars sheet (a photo or initials) beside the label and caption: no element per row.

geometry: the frame is sf-input's at sizes 1/2, 1, 2 -- the hairline, --sf-radius--ui, the block padding of each size and the inline padding plus the text inset -- so an empty lookup, a single one holding a value and sf-input of the same size are one height. Chips are sf-tag on the field's text line (line = size), so one row of chips keeps that height.

a11y: the combobox pattern of ARIA 1.2 with aria-activedescendant; the focus stays in the search box while the arrows move the active row, so a screen reader hears the row and typing goes on. Colours are role tokens: on-surface on the field and on the elevated list, on-surface-variant for captions, the hint, the placeholder and the state lines, primary-container for the active row, error for the error line -- the pairs the theme makes AA in light and dark.
css-variables: eight public variables, sf-input's seven in the field's pattern (§6) and the list's background, listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-lookup to choose people or objects from a set the host searches -- members of a chat, an assignee, a linked record -- or from a short list given whole.
do_not: Do not fetch inside the component or give it a URL: give it a provider function and answer {items, nextCursor} or {status: 'unavailable'}
Do not trust the submitted values on the server: check that the person may choose them
Do not use it for a fixed list of a few words without search; use sf-dropdown, sf-radio or sf-button-group
Do not use it for site search; use sf-search
ai_guidance.minimal_example:
<sf-lookup label="Members" name="members" multiple max-items="49"></sf-lookup>
<script>document.querySelector('sf-lookup').provider = async (query, {cursor, limit, signal}) => (await fetch(`/api/people?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&limit=${limit}`, {signal})).json();</script>

keyboard: Typing searches; ArrowDown opens the list and moves down, ArrowUp moves up, Home and End go to the ends while it is open
Enter chooses the active row; in a single field it closes the list
Escape closes the list; a second Escape clears the query
Backspace in the empty search box removes the last chip
Tab reaches each chip's remove button and leaves the field
accessibility.focus: Focus stays in the search box while the list is open; the active row is said through aria-activedescendant. The frame draws the focus ring while the box has keyboard focus; a click into it draws none. Removing a chip gives focus back to the search box.

search.summary: Puts a query in the search box and searches it as typing does, at once (no debounce), opening the list. Returns false while disabled or read-only.

retry.summary: Repeats the last call to the provider, with its query and cursor, as the Retry button does. Returns false when there is nothing to repeat.

close.summary: Closes the list and drops a search still running; the query stays.
